name: Module 6: bulk omics from adherent cells (metabolome + proteome from one extraction)
description: Bulk-omics chip: metabolome AND proteome from ONE cold acidified organic extraction of ADHERENT cells, in place on the chamber floor, before any encapsulation. 30 x 20 mm, ONE fluidic layer at ONE etch depth of 0.3 mm, resin print + hot emboss, geometry only from contracts/blocks.json (culture_chamber, centipede_channel). Three lanes (neurons, glia, astrocytes) that never share a wetted path: each lane is one culture field (1.2 x 8 x 0.3 mm, 2.88 uL), one inlet comb, one outlet comb, one inlet port and one outlet port. WHY ADHERENT CELLS AND NOT CAPSULES. A 70 um GelMA capsule at 5% w/v holds about 9 ng of gelatin against about 0.2-0.3 ng of protein in the cell inside it, so capsule gelatin outweighs the cell's protein roughly 30-45x and GelMA is itself protein: proteomics on capsules would measure the capsule. Native cytosolic protein could also leak out through the shell before the solvent denatures it (unmeasured). Extracting from adherent cells has no gelatin background, is published practice (direct cold solvent on adherent cells beat scrape-in-buffer 7x, Dettmer 2011 doi 10.1007/s00216-010-4425-x; a brief rinse then cold methanol minimises leakage, Kapoore 2017 doi 10.1039/C7AN00207F; one extraction giving proteins and metabolites, SIMPLEX, Coman 2016 doi 10.1074/mcp.M115.053702; supernatant for metabolites then the pellet digested for protein, Sapcariu 2014 doi 10.1016/j.mex.2014.07.002; a quick rinse roughly doubles detected features, Lorenz 2011 doi 10.1021/ac103313x) and it removes the retention problem, because a 25 um weir gap cannot be printed at the 200 um in-plane floor. The TRANSCRIPTOME ARM IS UNAFFECTED: it stays on capsules through module 4. This chip is the bulk arm only. FLOW, PER LANE. Seed and culture the adherent cells in the field (cell-adhesion coat on the field floor only, masked off the combs, so stray cells do not stay in the comb: untested). Brief ice-cold volatile-buffer rinse (mandatory). Stop-flow cold acidified organic quench in place, chloroform-free acetonitrile/methanol/water, cells lysed where they sit. Collect FRACTION 1 = METABOLOME out of the outlet; small peptides under about 10 kDa do not precipitate and land in this fraction, not the protein one. Resolubilise the precipitated protein left on the chamber floor with a denaturing solubilisation buffer. Collect FRACTION 2 = PROTEOME out of the SAME outlet at a later time. The protein is denatured by design: native complexes and enzyme activity are lost; bottom-up identification and quantification are not. Chloroform is OUT (it attacks PMMA and swells COC, risky for our materials). Fraction 1 is neutralised the moment it is collected (the vial is pre-charged off chip), because acid plus organic is only safe for RNA and acid-labile metabolites briefly. COMBS (the quench-speed fix). The old 20 s figure came from sweeping solvent along the long axis. Here the field is fed and drained through INTERDIGITATED COMBS along its two long edges, each a centipede_channel (a spine with short side branches): an inlet comb on the left edge (spine 0.8 mm wide, 13 teeth of 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch) and an outlet comb on the right edge with 13 teeth offset by half a pitch (0.3 mm), so teeth alternate along the 8 mm edge. Teeth are 0.2 mm wide with 0.4 mm ribs, meeting the 0.4 mm wall floor exactly. The inlet port sits at the top end of the left spine and the outlet port at the bottom end of the right spine (Z layout), so every tooth pair sees about the same total path. Flow then crosses the field's SHORT dimension, 1.2 mm, not its 8 mm length, so displacement time no longer depends on chamber length. Per unit flow, sweeping the long axis would need about 44x the pressure (path squared) and 6.7x the floor shear. A resistor-network model of this lane (Hele-Shaw field plus rectangular-duct teeth and spines, mu = 2.5 mPa s for the cold quench solvent) gives 1.37e+10 Pa s/m3, tooth flows from 0.61 to 2.02 of the mean (uneven; a wider spine evens it but adds extract volume), and wetted volume 11.444 uL per lane (field 2.88, each comb 3.28, plus 1 uL stub at each port: 0.5 uL hole through the lid plus an assumed 0.5 uL off-chip valve stub). The quench floods 2 wetted volumes (22.888 uL) in about 1 s (1373.3 uL/min): that is 314 Pa across the lane plus about 3.7 kPa across 100 mm of 0.5 mm bore line, total well under 10 kPa. Solvent first reaches the field after about 0.19 s (comb and stub volume), the field is flooded after about 0.38 s and the slowest tooth region after about 0.61 s; with wall-layer replacement and lysis the effective quench is about 0.5-1 s. Shell diffusion is not involved (cells are bare). Do NOT freeze-quench with the Peltier: at 2-10 K/s it takes 6-30 s, slower than the flood. The Peltier only holds the collected extract cold, which improves ADP/ATP recovery by about 40-45% (doi 10.1007/s00216-019-02018-3). Note this displacement estimate is for an open slot with cells on the floor; tables for a packed capsule bed (14 mm 6.8 s, 7 mm 1.7 s, 3 mm 0.3 s at 10 kPa) do not apply, and what limits the flood here is delivering the volume (flow), not pressure. QUENCH SPEED, HONEST LIMIT. With a quench of about 1 s you lose only the fastest roughly 10-15% of a panel: ATP/ADP, phosphocreatine, NAD(P)H, PEP/3PG and acyl-CoAs. Amino acids, TCA acids and lipids are safe. That holds ONLY if the rinse is short: held to the culture shear ceiling the rinse takes about 12 min in cold buffer (see SHEAR), which perturbs metabolism more than the quench saves. Until the rinse is shortened, treat ATP/ADP and glycolytic intermediates as invalid and TCA intermediates as provisional. EXTRACT VOLUME IS THE DESIGN RULE. The lever for metabolomics is extract volume, not cell count. Each fraction is collected at about 8.594 uL (1.2 x field + outlet comb + stub), so about 9,600 cells in 8.594 uL is about 1,117 cells/uL and a 2-5 uL injection is about 2,234-5,585 cell-equivalents. Keep the extract at or below about 10 uL, ideally the pore volume plus a little. Do not grow field area if the extract grows in proportion: concentration (cells/uL) then never improves, because field volume per cell is fixed by the 0.3 mm depth. Shrink spine width, teeth and stubs (the overhead) before adding area. PORT ALLOCATION (6 of 6). in_n, out_n, in_g, out_g, in_a, out_a. Each inlet sits behind its OWN off-chip selector valve (cell suspension, culture medium, cold rinse, cold quench, solubilisation buffer: five positions). Each outlet sits behind its OWN off-chip fraction collector, a three-position valve: waste, vial M (metabolome), vial P (proteome). The SECOND collection is a second fraction out of the SAME port at a different time. HOW THE TWO FRACTIONS STAY APART: the valve is at waste while rinse, quench flood, and the solvent flush run; it turns to vial M only for the extract chase; it returns to waste for the flush of 3 wetted volumes (34.332 uL) of solubilisation buffer, which clears the port hole, the stub and the lane of fraction 1; then it turns to vial P for the protein chase. Separate vials and separate valve ports mean fractions never share a vial. Nothing from one lane reaches another lane's valve, vial or line; only clean reagent reservoirs are shared upstream of the valves, each behind a check valve. CARRY-OVER RISK. Fraction 1 into fraction 2: after fraction 1 the stub holds about 1 uL of extract; the waste flush is 34 stub volumes (exp(-34) is negligible), but the lane itself keeps at most exp(-3) = 5% of the old solvent and its metabolites under ideal mixing (a laminar slot displaces better; unmeasured, to be shown with a dye test). That residue adds a little organic solvent and small metabolites to fraction 2, which bottom-up proteomics tolerates. Fraction 2 into fraction 1: none, because 2 comes later. Precipitate fines can pass into fraction 1 if the flood strips the floor film (mean floor shear in the flood is about 5 dyn/cm2, hottest tooth about 10); spin vial M and add its pellet to fraction 2. Dead-end valve ports do not mix ideally, so every bound is a design bound, not a measurement. SHEAR. The 0.01 dyn/cm2 culture ceiling applies to the steps with LIVING adherent cells: seeding, culture exchange and the cold rinse. It is held on the field with 15% headroom and the hottest tooth region (about 2.0x the mean) held to it, giving 3.78 uL/min for culture (mu 0.8 mPa s at 37 C) and 1.93 uL/min for the rinse (mu 1.57 mPa s at 4 C). It does NOT apply to the quench flood, the extract chase, the solvent flush or the protein chase, which run after the cells are killed. Rinse cost: 2 wetted volumes (22.888 uL) take 12 min at the ceiling. A rinse-specific ceiling of 0.3 dyn/cm2 (half the published detachment onset of 0.6 dyn/cm2, doi 10.1039/b820380f) would bring that to about 20 s; MJ should decide. The combs are not culture: any cell there is not counted and its shear is not held to the ceiling. YIELD. Floor area 9.6 mm2 per lane; at an ASSUMED 1,000 cells/mm2 (1e5 per cm2, a dense monolayer; sparser lineages such as neurons may give 2-3x fewer) that is about 9,600 cells per lane, 28,800 for the chip. Proteomics is comfortable at this input: 1,000 cells already gives 500-1,000 proteins (Mueller 2020 doi 10.15252/msb.20199111), so about 10x headroom. Metabolomics: the old 1e5-1e6 cell figure describes conventional 2.1 mm-column workflows. On nanoflow HILIC or CE-MS, 100 cells gave 1,620 peak pairs (doi 10.1021/acs.analchem.7b03100); roughly 1e3 cells gives 40-100 identified metabolites, 1e4 gives 100-160, 1e5 gives 200-300; AMP/ADP/ATP are seen from 500 cells by CE-MS (doi 10.1016/j.jchromb.2018.12.004). So about 1e4 cells is usable untargeted coverage of roughly 100-160 metabolites, provided the extract stays at or below about 10 uL. Medium: the field holds 2.88 uL of medium against about 0.019 uL of intracellular volume (assumed 2 pL per cell), about 150:1, or about 596:1 counting combs and stubs, so the rinse is not optional: it is what makes medium-borne metabolites (amino acids, glucose) measurable; metabolites absent from medium (nucleotides, phosphorylated glycolytic intermediates) are unaffected. UNTESTED. Whether the flood strips the precipitated protein film; whether the field-only adhesion coat keeps the combs cell-free; tooth flow uniformity (model only); whether COC tolerates the quench and solubilisation reagents over the contact time (compatibility is still TODO in contracts/materials.json); the 0.4 mm ribs between teeth (the floor, with no margin). Untargeted metabolomics at this input needs the nanoflow or CE-MS platform, not a conventional column.

chambers.note: Neurons lane culture field for ADHERENT cells, 1.2 x 8 x 0.3 mm, 2.88 uL, floor area 9.6 mm2 (about 9,600 cells at an assumed 1,000/mm2). No retention feature: the cells are attached to the floor. Fed from its left long edge by the inlet comb and drained at its right long edge by the outlet comb, so flow crosses the 1.2 mm short dimension. The quench, then the protein resolubilisation, happen here, in place.

channels.note: Neurons inlet comb: a 0.8 mm spine along the left long edge from the top-end port downwards, with 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch (0.4 mm ribs) opening into the field. Carries cell suspension, medium, rinse, quench and solubilisation buffer, one at a time.

Neurons outlet comb: 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm offset half a pitch from the inlet teeth, gathering into a 0.8 mm spine that drains to the bottom-end port. Both fractions leave through it, at different times.

Glia inlet comb: a 0.8 mm spine along the left long edge from the top-end port downwards, with 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch (0.4 mm ribs) opening into the field. Carries cell suspension, medium, rinse, quench and solubilisation buffer, one at a time.

Glia outlet comb: 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm offset half a pitch from the inlet teeth, gathering into a 0.8 mm spine that drains to the bottom-end port. Both fractions leave through it, at different times.

Astrocytes inlet comb: a 0.8 mm spine along the left long edge from the top-end port downwards, with 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm at 0.6 mm pitch (0.4 mm ribs) opening into the field. Carries cell suspension, medium, rinse, quench and solubilisation buffer, one at a time.

Astrocytes outlet comb: 13 side teeth 0.2 x 1.5 mm offset half a pitch from the inlet teeth, gathering into a 0.8 mm spine that drains to the bottom-end port. Both fractions leave through it, at different times.
